messages:
sahil: Heads up — after the host driver update (NVIDIA 535.86) our nsys traces for the KV-cache hot path look wrong. We get kernel timelines but no CUPTI CUDA API activity or NVTX ranges around the cache lookup code.
marie: hmm, do you see any errors when starting nsys? command you ran?
sahil: Ran: `nsys profile -t cuda,cudnn,cupti,osrt -o /tmp/serve_trace ./serve_bench --workload kvcache` — nsys completes, output file exists, but `nsys stats` shows zero CUPTI events. nsys stdout had this snippet: `cupti: failed to subscribe: CUPTI_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGES`
kai: version matrix pls (nsys / driver / cuda runtime inside container). Also are you profiling inside k8s/Docker?
sahil: nsys 2023.5.1, driver 535.86, container image uses cudatoolkit 12.1. Profiling inside docker (nvidia runtime). I did not run container privileged.
amanda: CUPTI/driver combo is super picky. In containers you often need --privileged or at least CAP_SYS_PTRACE + access to the host's CUDA driver libs. Try mounting /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI or use the host toolkit.
sahil: Tried `--cap-add=SYS_PTRACE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined` — same error. Also tried mounting /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcupti.so.12 from host into container, still no CUPTI events.
marie: Could be nsys expecting exact cupti library symbol versions. Did you try matching the nsys packaged CUDA toolkit? Newer driver may drop backward compatibility for certain CUPTI subscription APIs.
sahil: Also noticed kernel selection heuristics look different post-update: many small kernels got fused into a single big kernel on timeline, and our batching heuristics no longer line up with the KV-cache lookup hotspots. Pinpointing whether missing CUPTI events are causing bad kernel aggregation or vice versa.
kai: As a quick repro, can you add explicit NVTX ranges around the KV-cache lookup so we can at least identify where those ops land in the timeline even without CUPTI API events? e.g. `nvtxRangePushA(\"KV_LOOKUP\"); do_lookup(); nvtxRangePop();`
sahil: Good idea — added NVTX markers and retried. Now timeline shows NVTX ranges but still no CUPTI API rows. Perf regression still present: token latency p50 increased ~12% after driver update (from local perf test).
perf-bot: auto-check: compared 2026-02-24 baseline -> current driver change. KV cache CPU-GPU roundtrips up by +18%.
amanda: Two-pronged approach: 1) Try nsys host-side (run profiler on host binary referencing host's libcupti). 2) Test nsys 2024.1 (newer) and nsys 2023.4 (older) — different nsys binaries ship different CUpti link behaviors. Also try `--capture-range=nvtx` to force capture around NVTX ranges.
sahil: Ran host-side nsys (no container) with sudo — CUPTI events show up. So container boundary is suspect. Running with `--privileged` in container also made CUPTI initialize and capture events.
kai: That suggests container capabilities / toolkit mismatch. For k8s we should avoid privileged. Two options: 1) mount host cupti shared objects into the pod init container path and LD_PRELOAD them; 2) run a lightweight host agent (privileged) that triggers nsys attach, writes trace to a shared volume. Which is less invasive?
marie: Host agent seems safer operationally — we can restrict it to debug nodes. But we should also update our profiling docs to call out required caps and versions so engs don't get bitten.
sahil: Filed quick follow-up: I'll add NVTX instrumentation around KV cache, run a controlled perf test with host-side nsys to map exact kernels to cache ops, and open an infra ticket to prototype a host-side profiler agent. Also will test nsys 2024.1 to see if it avoids privileged requirement.
amanda: One more: add a small test that reproduces `CUPTI_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGES` (minimal repro) so we can share with NVIDIA if needed. Might be driver bug.
sahil: Yep — I'll attach traces + repro to the infra ticket. For immediate perf triage, using host-profiling + NVTX lets us confirm the KV cache hotspot is in index lookup kernel that is now larger due to driver-level kernel fusion. We can tune batch heuristics to split that kernel (workaround) while tracking driver fix. :thumbsup:
